batchName: Empire: Tiberius and Caligula (AD 14-41) - Easy Batch 2

questions.question: What did Germanicus recover from the Germans who had destroyed three legions in the Teutoburg Forest?
options: All the captured Roman prisoners
The body of the fallen Roman general
The pay chests of the three legions
Two of the three lost eagle standards
questions.explanation: Germanicus won back two of the three lost eagles, the legions' sacred standards. He also visited the battlefield and began burying the dead soldiers' remains.
questions.sourceQuote: Germanicus visited the battlefield, began burying the soldiers' remains, and recovered two of the three lost eagles (*aquilae*), the sacred standards of the legions.

questions.question: What does the nickname "Caligula" mean?
options: Little boot
Little soldier
Little Caesar
Little general
questions.explanation: As a toddler in Germany, Gaius wore a miniature uniform with little army boots (caligae), so the soldiers called him Caligula. He was the son of the general Germanicus.
questions.sourceQuote: As a toddler on campaign in Germany he wore a miniature uniform with little army boots (*caligae*), and the soldiers nicknamed him Caligula, "little boot".

questions.question: What happened to Caligula in the autumn of AD 37, only months into his reign?
options: He fell gravely ill for about a month
He was briefly deposed by the Senate
He led an army across the Rhine
He survived a Praetorian assassination plot
questions.explanation: Caligula hovered near death for about a month. After he recovered, the killings began.
questions.sourceQuote: In the autumn of AD 37, only months into his reign, the emperor Caligula fell gravely ill and hovered near death for about a month.

questions.question: According to ancient writers, what office did Caligula plan to give his racehorse Incitatus?
options: Praetorian prefect
Senator
Governor of Syria
Consul
questions.explanation: Ancient writers say Caligula planned to make Incitatus ("Speedy") a consul, one of Rome's two highest annual officials. Most modern historians see this as a joke at the expense of senators who craved the honour.
questions.sourceQuote: Ancient writers say he planned to make it a consul, one of Rome's two highest annual officials.

questions.question: What did Sejanus command as praetorian prefect?
options: The Praetorian Guard
The Rhine legions
The legions of Syria
The fleet at Misenum
questions.explanation: From AD 15 Sejanus commanded the Praetorian Guard, the emperor's bodyguard. That post became the base of his enormous power.
questions.sourceQuote: Sejanus became praetorian prefect (*praefectus praetorio*) in AD 15, commanding the Praetorian Guard (*cohortes praetoriae*), the emperor's bodyguard.

questions.question: How do many modern historians now view Caligula?
options: As a puppet controlled by his praetorian prefect
As a young man with near-limitless power and a cruel wit
As a wise reformer slandered by his enemies
As a genuine lunatic driven mad by his illness
questions.explanation: Many historians see a young man given near-limitless power, with a cruel sense of humour and open contempt for the Senate, rather than a madman. There is no reliable evidence of his mental state.
questions.sourceQuote: Many historians now see not a lunatic but a young man handed near-limitless power, with a cruel sense of humour and open contempt for the Senate.

questions.question: In AD 26, Tiberius left Rome for good. Where did he go?
options: Capri
Rhodes
Sardinia
Sicily
questions.explanation: Tiberius retired to his villas on Capri, an island in the Bay of Naples. With the emperor away, Sejanus ran the state.
questions.sourceQuote: In AD 26 Tiberius left Rome for good, retiring to his villas on Capri, an island in the Bay of Naples.

questions.question: Which honour did Tiberius refuse on becoming emperor?
options: A seat in the Senate
Command of the Rhine legions
The title Father of the Fatherland
The title first citizen (princeps)
questions.explanation: Tiberius turned down the title Father of the Fatherland and the Civic Crown, an oak-leaf wreath. He did accept the modest title of princeps, which the Senate confirmed in September AD 14.
questions.sourceQuote: He refused the title Father of the Fatherland (*pater patriae*) and the Civic Crown (*corona civica*), an oak-leaf wreath of honour.

questions.question: How did Caligula begin his reign in AD 37?
options: Exiled the senators who had served Tiberius
Invaded Britain and annexed its southern tribes
Cut the Guard's pay to refill the treasury
Gave cash to every citizen and staged lavish games
questions.explanation: Caligula's start was dazzling: cash handouts, lavish games and a doubled bonus for the Guard. A Jewish writer later called his first seven months a "Golden Age".
questions.sourceQuote: He doubled the Guard's bonus, gave cash to every citizen and staged lavish games.

questions.question: How did Tiberius become the stepson of Augustus?
options: His mother divorced his father and married Augustus
Augustus adopted him after his father died in battle
Augustus raised him as a hostage from the Claudii
His father married Augustus's widowed sister
questions.explanation: When Tiberius was a small child, his mother left his father and married Augustus. Tiberius himself came from the Claudii, one of Rome's oldest aristocratic families.
questions.sourceQuote: When he was a small child, his mother divorced his father and married Augustus, the man who would become Rome's first emperor.
